cells.tense: what you made from the first spark is here in your hands, and you're still moving with it.
cells.ask: let the next thing start before you know what it's for.
cells.core: You built something real out of what was only a maybe, and you still walk it forward. Nothing about that is loud. You hold what it became without gripping it, and you stay light enough to find the next step in the dark. The road isn't finished and you're not waiting for it to be.\n\nIt shows when you walk into a new situation with nothing to lean on yet. You don't force it into a shape you recognize, and you don't need the whole picture to move. You take the one step that's visible. The rest stays unknown until it comes to you, and you're fine letting it arrive that way.
cells.sheetLine: You made something real from the spark, and you're still walking it forward.
cells.place: in the low light where you move without seeing the whole road

cells.tense: you're already living at the end of something that hasn't finished happening.
cells.ask: see the one thing in front of you, just as it is, before you decide what it means.
cells.core: You're holding the whole finished shape of this before it's done being made — every way it could land, every judgment it might draw, already carried. Part of the weight you feel is weight you assigned to an ending that hasn't arrived. The road ahead keeps getting lit by a room you're not in yet.\n\nWhat works is when you look at one real piece of it and let that piece be exactly what it is. You keep the steps where you can actually take them, and the rest of the road stays out of sight. There's a kind of shining that comes from just being in the room, not from proving the room is right — that's the version of this that doesn't crush you. The ending will still be there when it's real. It doesn't need you living in it early.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying the ending as if it already happened.
cells.place: in the low light where you move without seeing the whole road

cells.tense: something grew past its early shape and you're still standing where it started.
cells.ask: let one thing in — see what it's become, not what it was going to be.
cells.core: The thing you were building has changed, or ended, or moved past where you left it. Standing on what it used to be keeps you behind it, in dim light, and the next step doesn't exist in the version you're holding. You keep looking for the old shape in a place it already left.\n\nWhen you're clear, you can look at a path just ahead and move without the whole map. You let what's actually there reach you, and the knowing gets deeper the longer you look instead of snapping shut. Nothing has to be finished for you to receive it. It just has to be looked at again, and you're the one who can look.
cells.sheetLine: The thing moved on, and you're still at the starting line.
cells.place: in the low light where you move without seeing the whole road

cells.tense: you're moving through what doesn't show any signs, and calling the movement the road's.
cells.ask: own one choice you've been making that you've been treating as just how it goes.
cells.core: You're already steering through uncertain ground — choosing which step to take, reading what's shifting, making calls where there's no clear answer. The steering is running the whole time. What's missing is the saying-so. You keep the fog between you and the fact that you're the one moving.\n\nWhen you're clear, you can stand in the middle of a situation with no fixed shape and move without waiting for the shape to arrive. You take the step that's visible, and you know your own read is what's carrying it forward. Nothing has to be named a decision for it to be yours. You just have to stop handing it to the fog.
cells.sheetLine: You're already choosing in the fog, and calling it following.
cells.place: in the low light where you move without seeing the whole road
